help.title: Zeroing
help.what: The work zero is the point a program counts from. Zeroing puts it where the tool is standing — usually after jogging down onto the corner of the stock.
help.moves: The machine does not move. Only the work reading changes; the machine position stays what it was.
help.system: The panel sends G10 L20 P<n>, where <n> is the active coordinate system: G54 is 1, G59 is 6. It will not guess that number — zeroing the wrong system gives no sign at all, and shows up when a tool moves to the wrong place under power.
help.choose: The keys under the readings switch the coordinate system the machine works in (G54–G59). Switching moves nothing and writes nothing to the controller's memory — each system keeps its own zero. A reset puts Grbl back in G54.
help.dead: The buttons are dimmed for two reasons: the controller has not reported a coordinate system, or the machine is in alarm — in alarm the server drops every G-code line before it reaches the cable.

homing.title: Homing
homing.axes: Grbl homes every axis at once ($H). One axis at a time only on controllers that can.

help.title: MDI
help.what: One line at a time, straight to the controller: a G-code block or one of Grbl's $ commands. It goes through the server's queue like any other line and is kept in the journal. Nothing asks for confirmation.
help.console: Above the line is the machine's console: every line sent to the controller, from any device, and every answer, each with its time. An error or an alarm shows its meaning beside the code.
help.alarm: In alarm the controller takes only $ commands — $X to unlock, $H to home. Any other line is refused and stays in the console struck through. While a program runs the line is off.
help.history: The line sent before, and back — this device's, until the page is reloaded
help.suggest: Opens the suggestions; they also open by themselves as you type a word
help.pick: With the suggestions open: choose one and put it in the line
help.sendButton: Sends the line, as Enter does
help.clearButton: Empties the console on this device; the journal keeps everything

app.certWarning: This authority is limited to names on your own network — it cannot vouch for any site on the internet. Even so, install it only for a machine you own, on a network you own.
app.certLife: The authority lasts a year, the server’s own certificate 30 days. The server replaces its own; after a year the authority stops working and a new one has to be installed, and the old one deleted in the phone’s settings — an expired one does not go away by itself.

certHow.android: Android: choose “CA certificate” rather than “VPN and app certificate”, and set a screen lock first if you have none.
certHow.ios: iPhone / iPad: install the downloaded profile in Settings, then under General → About → Certificate Trust Settings turn on full trust for this authority.
certHow.windows: Windows: open the downloaded file, “Install Certificate”, choose “Current User” and the “Trusted Root Certification Authorities” store.
certHow.macos: macOS: open the downloaded file in Keychain Access, add it to the “login” keychain, and set its trust to “Always Trust”.
certHow.linux: Linux: in the browser’s settings, Privacy and security → Certificates → Authorities, import the downloaded file and trust it for websites.

advice.noServer: The panel cannot reach its server. Check that it is running, which host this panel is pointed at, and -- if it is served over HTTPS -- whether the certificate has expired: a browser will not say which of those it is.
advice.alarm: Home the machine, or unlock it, before anything will move. Until then the server sends nothing at all.
advice.attaching: A port is open and the panel is attaching to it. Nothing to do but wait a moment.
advice.noPort: No port is open. Choose one and connect.
advice.resetFirst: A move went past an axis limit. Press Reset, then home the machine. Until then the controller takes nothing, homing and unlocking included.
advice.alarmInProgram: The alarm stopped a program. Stop it first — only then can the machine be unlocked or homed. Until then the server sends nothing.
advice.reportInches: The controller reports in inches ($13=1) and the server reads millimetres: positions, limits and moves are wrong. Fix it before moving the machine.

alerts.noDetail: The panel has nothing more specific to say about it.

stateHelp.paused: The program was paused by the server, not by the controller: the server stopped sending lines, and Grbl finished what was in its buffer and is standing still. A program stops like this on M6 (tool change), on an error in the file, or after the Pause button. You may jog and zero; Resume sends the rest, Abort ends the program.
stateHelp.title: States
stateHelp.alarm: The machine will not move until it is homed or unlocked. The panel will not unlock it by itself — the Unlock button in the Commands card does, when you say so, because that gives an unreferenced machine permission to move, and what is on the other end of the cable is your business.
stateHelp.door: A hold that arrived from outside — a guard, or an interlock. It looks like an alarm and is not: the machine resumes, and commands are sent as usual.
stateHelp.note: Alarm is the only state in which the server refuses to send — for Grbl, Smoothie and TinyG it drops the line rather than handing it to the machine, and the controls that would write are switched off while it lasts. Marlin has no notion of alarm at all: the gate is there in the code and always lets the line past, so nothing is ever held back on one.
stateHelp.noServer: The panel cannot reach its server — and so cannot reach the machine, which the server drives. It retries by itself every five seconds.
stateHelp.connecting: The panel is establishing its link to the server. A moment at startup and after any break.
stateHelp.noPort: The server is up, but no port is open. The machine may well be powered — nobody is listening to it.
stateHelp.attaching: The port is open and the panel is attaching to it. A fraction of a second, with nothing to do.
stateHelp.noReading: The panel is attached, but the machine has not said anything about itself yet. Not the same as Idle: Idle is the firmware speaking, this is silence. Commands do leave the server for the port — for the cable, not for the machine: with nothing answering, there is no way to tell whether anything is receiving them. Normally gone within a quarter of a second; if it stays, there is no controller on the other end.
stateHelp.unknown: A state reported by the firmware. The panel shows it exactly as it arrived.
stateHelp.noStates: This controller reports no machine state at all. The panel will read “No reading” for the whole session — that is not a fault.
stateHelp.idle: The machine is standing still and waiting. Commands go straight out.
stateHelp.run: The machine is moving under a program.
stateHelp.jog: A manual move, started from this panel or another.
stateHelp.home: Homing — the machine is looking for its limit switches.
stateHelp.hold: Feed hold. Motion has stopped and can be resumed.
stateHelp.check: Program check. The firmware reads the G-code and does not run it — nothing moves.
stateHelp.sleep: Asleep. The axis drivers are off and the position is lost; it takes a reset.
stateHelp.initializing: The controller is still starting up.
stateHelp.stop: Stopped by M0 or M1, waiting to be resumed.
stateHelp.end: The program reached its end — M2 or M30.
stateHelp.interlock: Safety interlock — the circuit is open. Nothing moves until it closes.
stateHelp.shutdown: The controller shut down after a critical fault. The panel still sends — it is TinyG refusing, until a reset.
stateHelp.panic: A critical failure. The panel still sends; TinyG will take nothing before a reset.
stateHelp.alarmGrbl: The machine will not move until it is homed or unlocked. Opening the port resets Grbl, and with homing enabled ($22=1) that is exactly how it comes up. The panel will not unlock it by itself — the Unlock button in the Commands card does, when you say so, because that gives an unreferenced machine permission to move, and what is on the other end of the cable is your business. After a STOP in motion (ALARM:3) the position is lost, and homing is the right way out.

machine.stepsChanged: Changing steps changes the scale of motion. After saving, check the work zero and home the machine.

bar.noAnswer: The controller did not confirm the write. Check the connection and the Journal.
bar.grblRefused: Grbl refused {{name}} ({{code}}): {{meaning}} The changes before it are already saved.

reportFix.wrong: The controller reports in inches ($13=1). The server reads every position as millimetres, so positions, limits and moves are wrong now. Put $13 back to 0.
reportFix.title: Report in millimetres again?
reportFix.note: The controller will store $13=0. Positions are right at once; the panel still shows inches if you chose them in Preferences.

history.title: History of changes
history.none: The server has not seen a change yet.
history.restoreNote: Restoring adds changes to save. They are written through the review.
history.importUnknown: Left out, the controller does not know them: {{names}}.
history.fileFailed: That did not work — check the connection to the server.

s0.title: Step pulse
s0.note: Length of the STEP pulse. Raise it if the drivers lose steps.

s1.title: Motor idle delay
s1.note: After this much idle time the motors are released. 255 = they always hold position.

s2.title: Invert STEP signal
s2.note: For drivers that act on the falling edge.

s4.title: Invert ENABLE signal
s4.note: When the motors are loose with the driver enabled.

s10.title: Status report
s10.note: The position in the report and the planner buffer. With the buffer the server knows more exactly which program line is running.

s11.title: Junction deviation
s11.note: Larger = faster through corners, smaller = more exact.

s12.title: Arc tolerance
s12.note: How exactly G2/G3 is divided into segments.

s13.title: Report in inches
s13.note: Locked Off. The server counts everything in millimetres — positions, limits, homing — and converts to inches itself if you choose them in Preferences. You lose nothing: the panel, jogging and files work in inches just the same, and reports in inches would only falsify those figures.

s20.title: Soft limits
s20.note: Refuses moves beyond the axis travel ($130–132).

s21.title: Limit switches
s21.note: A switch tripping stops motion and raises an alarm.

s22.title: Homing
s22.note: Needs a $H cycle after every start. A condition for soft limits — turning it off turns $20 off too.

s23.title: Homing direction
s23.note: The side the switches are on

s24.title: Locate feed
s24.note: The slow second approach that sets the position.

s25.title: Seek feed
s25.note: The fast approach to the switch.

s26.title: Switch debounce
s26.note: How long a switch signal takes to settle.

s27.title: Pull-off
s27.note: Distance after homing, so the switch is not left pressed.

s30.title: Max speed
s30.note: The S value that means full PWM.

s31.title: Min speed
s31.note: The lowest speed; smaller S is raised to it.

s32.title: Laser mode
s32.note: Power follows speed, with no stops on M3/M4.

check.softWithoutHoming: Soft limits are on but homing is off. GRBL will not use them.
check.pullOffLong: The pull-off after homing ({{value}} {{unit}}) is more than 10% of the shortest axis.
check.seekSlower: The seek rate is slower than the locate rate.
check.hardOff: Limit switches off: outside homing they will not stop motion.

geo.unplaced: Homing is off: the size of the travel is known, its place is not. Machine zero is wherever the machine stood at power-on.

review.title: Changes to save ({{count}})
review.note: An EEPROM write takes effect at once and stays after power-off. Values go in this order; the first refused stops the rest. The previous values stay in the change history.
review.bad: Correct the invalid values before saving.

confirm.eeprom: Written to the controller's EEPROM. The change takes effect at once and survives a power-off.

caution.title: Homing is off
caution.where: Machine zero is wherever the machine stood at power-on, so where its travel lies is not known. Only its size is.
caution.guards: Nothing guards the ends of the axes: Grbl has no soft limits then, and the panel does not clip jogging. A move from MDI or a program goes as far as it is told.
caution.moves: "Go to zero" and go-to-point are off: there is no known top of Z to lift to, and no certain point on the drawing.
caution.fix: Homing is switched on in Settings → Controller → Homing ($22). It needs limit switches.

probe.title: Probe
probe.remember: Kept from last time. Check them, change what differs — they are kept again for next time.

method.cornerNote: Corner of the work: X0, Y0 and Z0, with an L-shaped plate.
method.paperNote: By hand with a sheet of paper: the top or any side, no probe.
method.mapNote: A grid of points by probe: the program follows a warped board. The zero stays as it is.
method.measureNote: A circle, a rectangle or a width, with the probe: its size and middle — and, if you want, the zero there.

how.paper: Hold a sheet of paper between the tool and the surface you chose. Nothing needs clipping — the machine moves only when you jog.

lay.z: Lay the plate flat on the work, under the tool.
lay.corner: Set the L plate on the chosen corner, its walls against both edges of the work.
lay.hole: Plug the 3D probe into the probe input instead of the plate.

place.z: Jog the tool over the plate, a few millimetres above it — less than the Z travel limit.
place.corner: Jog the tool over the plate, a few millimetres above it and about 8 mm in from both walls.
place.paper: Bring the tool a few millimetres over the surface chosen — in front of it for a side. Keep the sheet at hand.
place.hole: Lower the probe's ball into the hole, a few millimetres below its edge, roughly in the middle — clear of the walls.
place.boss: Set the probe's ball over the middle of the part, a few millimetres above its top — less than the Z travel limit.
place.map: Raise the tool above the clamps, no higher than the Z reach limit over the board. X and Y do not matter: at this height the machine travels over the first point by itself and starts looking for the board.
place.groove: Lower the probe's ball into the groove, a few millimetres below its edge, roughly in the middle — clear of the walls.
place.bar: Set the probe's ball over the middle of the bar, a few millimetres above its top — less than the Z travel limit.
place.pocket: Lower the probe's ball into the pocket, a few millimetres below its edge, roughly in the middle — without touching the walls.
place.edge: Put the probe's ball over the part, a few millimetres in from the edge chosen and above the top — less than the clearance past the side and the Z travel limit.
place.slot: Lower the probe's ball into the slot, a few millimetres below its edge, roughly in the middle. The points' spacing must be well under the slot's width.
place.wall: Lower the probe ball into the pocket, a few millimetres under its edge, clear of the walls — it touches the chosen wall from inside at two points.
place.surface: Set the probe ball over the surface, a few millimetres above it — less than the Z travel limit.

corner.pickHow: Tap one of the four corners. The plate jumps to it; the arrows show which way each probe goes.

move.zFast: Z · fast move down to the plate
move.xFast: X · fast move to the wall
move.yFast: Y · fast move to the wall
move.zero: Zero written: Z0, X0 and Y0
move.depth: X · down beside the plate's wall

corner.overCode: G0 over where Z was touched

field.spacing: Spacing of the points on the edge

wire.how: Clip the lead to the tool. Touch the plate to the tool and let go. The panel reads the probe from the controller: it shows “Touching” while they touch and “Works” once you let go.
wire.unknown: The controller does not report its inputs, so the wire cannot be checked here.
wire.untested: The wire is untested. If the plate or the probe is not plugged in, the machine will travel all the way to the travel limit while measuring and only then stop with ALARM:5.
wire.picture: The clip on the tool, and the plate apart from it and touching it
wire.howHole: Deflect the probe's tip with a finger and let go. The panel reads the probe from the controller: it shows “Touching” while deflected and “Works” once you let go.
wire.probePicture: A 3D probe in the holder: at rest, and its tip pushed aside by a finger
wire.normallyClosed: If “Touching” shows while you are not pushing the tip, the probe is normally closed (NC). Invert the probe input: $6=1 in the controller settings. Without it the measurement stops at once with ALARM:4.
wire.howMap: Clip the lead to the tool and the other to the board's copper, or plug in a 3D probe. Touch and let go: the panel shows "Touch", then "Working".

position.clipOn: The probe input is lit: the plate is touching the tool, or the lead is shorted. Clear it before measuring.
position.notNow: The machine has to stand idle, with no program, to measure.

measure.note: The machine moves by itself now. STOP is at the top as always.

failure.notFound: {{axis}}: nothing was touched within the travel limit. Nothing was written. Check the plate or the probe and the lead, or move the tool closer.
failure.alreadyTouching: {{axis}}: the probe was already touching before the move. Nothing was written. Check the lead is not shorted.
failure.softLimit: The move would leave the machine travel (soft limits). Nothing was written. Reset, then move the tool or home the machine.
failure.touched: {{axis}}: the tool came down on the plate instead of beside it. Nothing was written. Increase “Out past the wall” or start closer to the corner.
failure.reset: The measurement was stopped. Nothing was written.
failure.positionLost: Since the measurement the machine may have lost its position, or was homed, so the result no longer holds. Nothing was saved. Measure again.
failure.noAnswer: The machine stands still and has not answered the measurement's line — the answer may have been lost on the cable. Nothing was saved. Check the connection and measure again.
failure.other: The measurement failed ({{code}}). Nothing was written.

result.note: Nothing is written until you save. Clear the plate, the paper or the probe away before cutting.

move.along: Point {{pass}} · along the side, over the top
move.setDown: Point {{pass}} · {{axis}}: set-up — down beside the side
move.fast: Point {{pass}} · {{axis}}: fast touch of the side
move.in: Point {{pass}} · {{axis}}: to the middle, across the side

edge.alongCode: G0 along the side to the point

phase.along: along the side to the point
phase.in: to the middle before the point

edge.inCode: G0 to the middle, across the side

plate.fast: Z · fast move down to the plate
plate.miss: No plate: down to the limit

paper.fine: {{axis}} · 0.1 mm steps, the sheet still free
paper.pickHow: Tap a side or the middle of the work. The sheet jumps to the surface chosen; the arrow shows which way the tool comes.
paper.feelHow: Put the sheet between the tool and the surface and slide it while stepping in by 0.1 mm, then 0.01 mm. When it drags — still moving, but pulling — that is “Here”. If it resists or stands, step back.

join.how: Join to run this measurement from here — the steps move together on both devices. A wizard of your own takes the measurement over once you reach Position in it.
join.taken: The wizard was taken over on {{where}}.
join.leaveNote: The wizard keeps waiting on {{where}} — finish it there, or join it here again.

hole.centreCode: G0 to the middle of the touches
hole.passesWhy1: One pass: 4 touches, half the time. The middle of any chord of a circle lies on its centre, so it is enough when the ball starts near the middle of the hole.
hole.passesWhy2: Two passes: the second from the centre the first found, its touches square to the walls. Surer when the start is far off the middle — then the first touches meet the wall at a slant.

move.topFast: Z · fast down to the top
move.setOut: Pass {{pass}} · {{axis}}: set up — past the side, over the top
move.setDown: Pass {{pass}} · {{axis}}: set up — down beside the side
move.fast: Pass {{pass}} · {{axis}}: fast touch of the side
move.topLift: Z · off, up to travel over the top

boss.outCode: G0 past the side, over the top

map.badArea: The area needs a width in X and in Y: "to" above "from".
map.badGrid: From 2 to 30 points on each axis.
map.start: Work coordinates, as the program's (0 is the current system's zero). The dashed line: the loaded program's extent.
map.note: Heights from the first point. Before you turn the map on at a program, set Z0 on the first point. Nothing is kept until you save it.
map.noServer: The server does not know the height map: it needs updating or a restart.

move.next: Fast touch at the next point
move.miss: Nothing under the tool: the limit and an ALARM
move.place: The plate under the tool, by hand

tool.boardNote: The lead on the tool, a wire to the board's copper.
tool.plateNote: Moved by hand to every point. The machine waits over the point.

map.placeAsk: Lay the Z plate under the tool, over point {{n}}, and press "Plate is there". The machine stands still.

mode.pointNote: A corner (typed or taken by jog), a width and a depth.
mode.cornersNote: Two corners across: typed, or taken by jog.
mode.centreNote: A centre (typed or taken by jog), a width and a depth.

map.takeCorners: Type both corners, or jog over one and press "Here", then over the corner across.
map.startDrawing: Side-on: the board between the clamps, the tool in the band above the clamps and under the Z reach limit

move.size: Size: the touches apart, and the ball
move.edge: Angle: from the two touches and their spacing
move.oval: Oval: the ellipse through eight touches
move.slot: Slot: the shape through eight touches
move.surface: Z: touched by the ball's lowest point

size.repeatsWhy1: One measurement: the size from the last pass.
size.repeatsWhyMore: Several measurements, each from the centre found: the size is their mean, with the spread (largest less smallest).
size.ball: The size rests on the ball diameter: {{ball}} {{unit}}.
size.note: The zero changes only with “Set zero”. The result is in the Journal.
size.offWhy: Out of round: the farthest touch from the middle less the nearest. Near zero, it is a circle; more, an oval, a shape at an angle or a flaw.
size.angleWhy: The angle from the axis, anticlockwise. Grbl does not rotate coordinates (no G68): square the part, or allow for the angle in the program.
size.codeTurned: sides and angle = from the lines through each side's touches
size.squareWhy: How far the sides across differ in angle from those along. Near zero, the corners are square; more, a rhombus, or a touch that met the next wall (make the spacing smaller).
size.codeOval: axes, angle and middle = the ellipse fitted to the touches, the ball taken off
size.offOvalWhy: Ovality: axes along X and Y — backlash, or one axis's steps per mm; axes near 45° — X and Y not square. How far off: the touches from the ellipse.
size.codeSlot: length, width, angle and middle = the slot fitted to the touches, the ball taken off
size.offSlotWhy: Off the slot: the touch farthest from the fitted slot less the nearest. Near zero, it is a slot; more, another shape, a flaw or a point too near an end.

kind.circleNote: A hole or a stud: diameter, middle and how far from round — or its ovality: the ellipse's two axes and their angle.
kind.rectNote: A pocket or a part, its sides along X and Y: sizes and middle.
kind.widthNote: A groove or a bar, along one axis: width and middle.
kind.edgeNote: A side of the part at two points: its angle to the axis and where the edge lies.
kind.slotNote: A slot with round ends, cut or standing, along the axes or turned: length, width, angle and middle.
kind.distanceNote: Between two features — holes, studs or edges: the distance, and for two centres X, Y and the angle too.
kind.angleNote: Two edges that meet: the angle between them, how far off square, and where the corner is.
kind.heightNote: A surface touched from above: its Z — or two: how far the second is higher or lower, e.g. a step's height, a pocket's depth.

distance.toSecond: First measured. Second: {{what}} — jog over to it.
distance.angle: Angle of the line of centres
distance.centresWhy: From the first centre to the second. X and Y differences: the second less the first. The line of centres from the X axis, anticlockwise.
distance.fromEdgeWhy: From the centre to the edge, square to it — also when the edge lies at an angle.
distance.edgesWhy: Square to the edges, the mean from both sides. Off parallel: how far the second edge is turned against the first.
distance.note: The zero is not changed. The result is in the Journal.

meet.angleWhy: The angle inside the part between the edges — with two pocket walls, inside the pocket. 90° — a square corner; off square is the difference from 90°.

height.dzWhy: The difference in machine Z between the touches: it does not depend on the tool's length or the ball. Negative — the second surface lower (a pocket's depth), positive — higher (a step's height).
height.zWhy: The Z of the ball's lowest point in the system — true if Z0 was set with the same probe. No zero is written from it: for a tool of another length it would be wrong.
height.note: The zero is not changed. The result is in the Journal.

wire.mustTest: Next unlocks once the probe input lights and goes out again: touch the plate to the tool, or push the probe's stylus aside and let go. Without that, with the lead off, the machine travels the whole limit.
wire.testHere: The lead is not tested on this device: touch the plate to the tool, or push the stylus aside and let go — Measure then unlocks.

surface.warn: Measured on: {{on}}, Z0 on: {{z0}} — the zero goes the stock's thickness away from where it is measured. After Save or Discard the choice goes back to where it is measured.

failure.touchedCorner: {{axis}}: the tool came down onto the plate instead of beside it. Nothing was saved. Increase the side travel from the start, or start nearer the corner.
failure.touchedProbe: {{axis}}: the probe touched the work on a move meant to pass it — a wall in the way, or coming down onto the part. Nothing was saved. Start nearer the middle or the edge, reduce the point spacing, or increase the clearance past the side.

method.probe3dNote: A zero with the 3D probe: the middle of a hole, a stud, a pocket or a part, an edge, a corner.
method.measureNote: Sizes with the 3D probe: a distance between features, a step's height or a pocket's depth.

kind.circleNote: The middle and diameter of a round hole or stud.
kind.rectNote: Sides along X and Y: the middle and size on both axes — or on one (a groove, a bar).
kind.edgeNote: A side of the part at two points: where the edge is, and its angle to the axis.
kind.cornerNote: A part's or a pocket's, from one start: both edges, where they meet and the angle between them.
kind.distanceNote: Between two features — holes, studs or edges — jogged between.
kind.heightNote: Two surfaces touched from above: how far the second is higher or lower, e.g. a step's height, a pocket's depth.

place.cornerOut: Bring the probe's ball over the part, a few millimetres in from both edges of the corner and over the top — less than the clearance past the side and the Z travel limit.
place.cornerIn: Lower the probe's ball into the pocket, a few millimetres under its edge and a few from both walls of the corner — not touching them.

move.alongGuarded: Point {{pass}} · along the side, inside — guarded

edge.alongGuardedCode: G38.3 along the side — a wall in the way stops it

move.corner: Corner: where the two edges meet

size.codeCorner: corner = where the lines through each edge's touches cross
